name: reviewer-create-change decide(rejected) → coordinator re-dispatch
description:
ADR-057 §D5 — the create-change reject recovery. Fires when reviewer-create-change rejects the draft for FIXABLE gaps (a dropped constraint, a weak scenario, a build-not-test task). Routes to the coordinator with the reviewer's concrete gaps; the coordinator re-dispatches a tightened create_change (a FRESH run with a new run entity — supersession-via-new-spawn, ADR-039 Shape A) or, if the gaps are not cleanly fixable, respond_direct/ask_user.

Why re-dispatch and not re-author in place: v1 emit_change is single-emit with NO remover (ADR-057 §Build addendum deferred-upsert coupling). Re-running the SAME author would append a second change.<slug>.* set onto the same run entity (stale-read hazard). A coordinator re-dispatch starts a new run, so the new change.* lands on a new entity — no collision. The in-place reviewer→author recovery loop (with the triple-remover upsert) is the deferred ADR-039 slice. max_iterations bounds re-dispatch thrash.

Distinct from rule 05 (needs_clarification): rejected = the draft has fixable gaps a fresh draft resolves; needs_clarification = the ASK is ambiguous and needs the user. Per-reason routing per [[feedback-rejected-to-coordinator]].

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
Create-change recovery. Reviewer-create-change at loop $entity.instance rejected the drafted change for fixable gaps. You are the senior thinker; decide how to recover.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result on $entity.instance to read the reviewer's verdict. The reason field names the CONCRETE gaps (a dropped constraint, a weak scenario, a build-not-test task). These are your re-dispatch instructions.

Iteration 2 — judge what to do:

- decide(action="create_change", reason=...) if a tightened re-draft can fix the gaps. Your reason MUST carry BOTH the original ask AND the reviewer's specific fixes folded in — the new author starts fresh and only sees your reason. Be concrete: name the dropped constraint and where it must land, name the weak scenario and what it must assert. This spawns a fresh author on a new run.
- decide(action="ask_user", reason=..., question=...) if a fixable re-draft needs a decision only the user can make. Ask one focused question.
- decide(action="respond_direct", reason=...) if the gaps are not cleanly fixable (the ask is out of scope, or the reviewer's bar cannot be met without information that does not exist). Be honest in your reason.

This recovery routes through you because you carry the strongest reasoning model; re-dispatch is bounded (max_iterations=3) so a chronically-rejected ask surfaces to the user rather than thrashing.

metadata.supersession_not_in_place: Re-dispatch (fresh run) not re-author (same run): v1 emit_change has no remover, so re-running the author would double-stamp change.<slug>.*. The deferred ADR-039 in-place loop adds the remover. See ADR-057 §Build addendum deferred-upsert coupling.
metadata.distinct_from_needs_clarification: rejected = fixable draft gaps → re-dispatch; needs_clarification (rule 05) = ambiguous ask → ask_user/respond. Per-reason routing.
